syntaxRules.statement: In most Bukharian words, except verbs, stress falls on the last syllable. If a suffix is added, the stress moves to the suffix.

syntaxRules.title: Hebrew-origin numbers

syntaxRules.statement: Compound numbers are joined with the conjunction -u after a consonant or -yu after a vowel. The higher number comes first, followed by the lower ones in order.

syntaxRules.title: Ordinal formation - suffix choice

syntaxRules.title: Jewish day boundary
syntaxRules.statement: The Jewish day runs from sunset to sunset, so Saturday begins on Friday evening (shavi shabot) and Sunday begins on Saturday evening (shavi yakshanbe).

syntaxRules.title: Possessive Rule 1 - consonant
syntaxRules.statement: If the noun ends in a consonant, add the suffix -i to the noun, followed by the pronoun (man, tu, u, mo, shumo, inho).

syntaxRules.title: POSSESSION

syntaxRules.title: Regular form rule

syntaxRules.title: Two forms for vowel stems

syntaxRules.title: Literal form rule

syntaxRules.title: Noun plural

syntaxRules.title: Literal form in writing

syntaxRules.title: Present continuous
syntaxRules.statement: The Present Continuous says something is happening at this very moment. It is built from the past participle of the main verb plus the auxiliary istodan, which carries the person and number.

syntaxRules.statement: Drop the last three letters of the infinitive, add sod (from the participle istoda), then add the conversational ending: raftan gives raf, then rafsodim, rafsodi, rafsoded, rafsode.

syntaxRules.title: Descriptive past
syntaxRules.statement: The Descriptive Past covers habitual or repeated past actions, English 'used to'. Take me-, add the verb without its infinitive ending, then add the ending. Negation is na- before me-.

syntaxRules.title: Compound verbs from nouns
syntaxRules.statement: A large class of verbs is a noun plus a common verb. The same noun can take different verbs for different meanings: rish giriftan is to shave, rish mondan is to grow a beard; zan giriftan is to marry, zan sar dodan is to divorce.

syntaxRules.title: Past perfect
syntaxRules.statement: The Past Perfect says something happened before another past action, or before a set time in the past. Take the past participle, put bud next to it, then add the ending.

syntaxRules.title: Past perfect endings

syntaxRules.title: Comparatives
syntaxRules.statement: Comparatives are formed by adding the suffix -tar to adjectives: kalon (big) gives kalontar (bigger), bad (bad) gives badtar (worse).

syntaxRules.title: Superlatives
syntaxRules.statement: Superlatives are formed by adding the suffix -in to the comparative form of adjectives: kalontar (bigger) gives kalontarin (the biggest), behtar (better) gives behtarin (the best).

syntaxRules.title: Ordinal superlatives
syntaxRules.statement: Adding -umin (after a consonant) or -yumin (after a vowel) to a cardinal number gives the very first, second and so on: yak gives yakum (first) and yakumin (the first).

syntaxRules.title: Present perfect tense
syntaxRules.statement: The Present Perfect expresses an action completed with respect to the present, at an unspecified time before now. It is used with expressions such as ever, never, once, many times, before, already, yet. It has two forms: Regular and Literal.

syntaxRules.title: Reflexive pronoun xud
syntaxRules.statement: Xud expresses both reflexivity and possession. As a reflexive pronoun it can come before or after the personal pronoun, and all forms can act as the subject. As a possessive, only the suffixed form is normally used, and it always follows the noun.

syntaxRules.title: Passive voice
syntaxRules.statement: Passive verbs use an auxiliary verb (shudan). The main verb appears as a past participle, formed by dropping the final -n from the infinitive: soxtan gives soxta shudan, zoyidan gives zoyida shudan.

syntaxRules.title: Passive of nominal compound verbs
syntaxRules.statement: For nominal compound verbs with the auxiliary kardan, the passive is formed by replacing kardan with shudan: garm kardan (to warm up) gives garm shudan (to become warm).

syntaxRules.title: Verbal compound verbs
syntaxRules.statement: Verbal compound verbs join two verbs that both keep their meaning, for synchronous or consecutive actions. The first verb takes the past participle and the second is conjugated as normal.

syntaxRules.title: Indefinite nouns
syntaxRules.statement: Bukhori has no special form for definite nouns. The indefinite noun is formed by adding the suffix -e to the noun (kas gives kase, mard gives marde, rüz gives rüze). In compound sentences -e comes before the conjunction ki, marking what follows as a defining subordinate clause.

syntaxRules.title: Past continuous tense
syntaxRules.statement: The Past Continuous is used for actions that were going on (not finished) at a particular time in the past. It has two forms, Regular and Literal.

syntaxRules.title: Past continuous - Literal form

e1508.bux: Ha, apa Tomor, naghzet, sahat hastet? Ma Freho a Irusholayim.
e1508.en: Oh, Tomor, how do you do? I'm Fareho from Jerusalem.
e1508.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1509.bux: Ha, apa Freho, dugonajon, hov-hov, tinji. Naghzet, chitüyet?
e1509.en: Oh, Fareho, dear friend, I'm all right. How are you?
e1509.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1510.bux: Borux Hashem! Famidam, ki duxtari xoleton shinixüri naveresha kardak. Morak shava! Naghz guzashtak?
e1510.en: Thank G-d! I heard that your cousin celebrated her grandson's engagement party.
e1510.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1511.bux: Hov, shinixüri haminxel xushrü bu, ki ma ba shumo gufta nametonam. Qariv sadu pinjo odam budan.
e1511.en: Yes, the engagement party was so nice that you can't even imagine. About 150 people attended.
e1511.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1512.bux: Hay-hay. Ino ki qati qudo shudan?
e1512.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1513.bux: Ino kelina a Buxoro griftin. Ma qudoshona nameshinosam. Megun, ki oilayi kelin boy-badavlat.
e1513.en: The bride is from Bukhara. I don't know their in-laws. People say that they are very rich.
e1513.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1514.en: What profession do the groom and the bride have?
e1514.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1521.bux: Kelin ba'di yak sol universitet tamom mekuna, düxtur meshü. Domot advakot. Korash bisyor sara. Safetbax boshan Elohim!
e1521.en: The bride will graduate from the university in a year. The groom is a lawyer. His job is very good. May they be happy!
e1521.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1522.en: Yes, may they be well! Did the relatives give any gifts?
e1522.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1523.bux: Chuva ne?! Padaru modari kelin domotba so'ati tilo, kostyumi zür dodin. Padaru modari domot kelinba halqayi brillionti kori kalon matono dodin. Himinxel varq zasode, ki man ba shumo gufta nametonam.
e1523.en: Why not?! The bride's parents gave the groom a gold watch and a nice suit as a gift. The groom's parents gave the bride wonderful diamond earrings as a gift. You can't even imagine how shiny they are.
e1523.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1524.bux: Hay-hay, 'ayn-oro dur boshan! Xay, bo chi?
e1524.en: Oh-oh, may they be far from an evil eye! What else?
e1524.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1525.bux: Ba'di hamin qoshchinon kardin. Vaqti qoshchinon Avromi Tolmas ashuli fash-fasha xondak. Ba esaton has in ashula?
e1525.en: Then the ceremony of eyebrow threading took place. During the ceremony Avrom Tolmas sang a Fash-fasha song. Do you remember it?
e1525.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1526.bux: Ibi, hov. Ba qoshchinoni ma, Xudo rahmat kuna, Nekqadami sozanda in ashulaya mexondak. Mana unvaxt ba kurti juuti püshonda budan.
e1526.en: Of course. The singer, Nekqadam, used to sing it at my ceremony, may her soul rest in peace. In the time of my ceremony I had dressed in a Jewish dress.
e1526.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1528.bux: Ba domotu kelinam livosoi buxori püshondin. Baroyi in rüzi murod bivi kelin kurti osin daroz düxtin.
e1528.en: A groom and a bride were dressed in the Bukharian dress as well. Especially on this happy occasion, the bride's grandmother sewed a long sleeve dress.
e1528.speaker: Tomor

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)
source.note: spoken by Tomor; speech continues on p82

e1540.bux: Kelin bisyor xushrü bu. Üya ba kurti osin daroz püshondin, boli sarash tüpi 'arüsi zarinu rümoli pulakcha püshondin. Boli sari domot tüpi zarinu salayi zarin püshondin va ba badanash jomayi zarin moghen Dovid qati püshondin. Duyashon du gul borin budan. Ba'd ino bozi kardan.
e1540.en: The bride was very beautiful. She was dressed in a long sleeve dress, she had a gold sewed bride's yarmulke on her head, and a spangled shawl. The groom was dressed in a goldthread embroidered yarmulke and a men's shawl on the head; he was wearing a goldthread embroidered caftan with David's stars on it. Both of them looked as pretty as flowers. Then they danced.
e1540.speaker: Tomor

e1541.bux: Vaqtam choq shu a in gav. Eloim ba ya bax piru kampir shavan!
e1541.en: I was happy to hear that. May they be together forever!
e1541.speaker: Fareho

source.section: dialogue (Chaqchaq, phone call Jerusalem - New York)

e1543.bux: Xay, naghz monet, Tomorjon. Shumoyam tüyi naveretona binet!
e1543.en: Ok. Be well, dear Tomor. May you also see the wedding of your grandson!
e1543.speaker: Fareho

e1806.bux: Bivijon, ma mexoyam, ki a shumo pursam va ba daftaram navisam, avloti mo a gujo, kiyo megun?
e1806.en: Dear grandmother, I want to ask you and write in my notebook: what is our background?
e1806.speaker: Navera

e1807.bux: Joni bivesh, chitü tu in gava mepursi?
e1807.en: Dear grandson, why do you ask this?
e1807.speaker: Bivi

e1808.bux: Ma alakay kalon shudam, mehoyam, ki famam avloti mo a gujo sar shu?
e1808.en: I've grown up already. I want to know who our family began from, and where we came from.
e1808.speaker: Navera

e1809.bux: Hay, biyo, shin yoni ma. Mana gush kun. Ma ba tu megum. Nomi bovom Elozor Simhoev bud. Ü dar shari Buxoro dar soli 1840 ba oili Simhoyu Rivqo zoyda shuda bud. Pesh, odamo familiya nadoshtan. A broyi ki, dadeshon Simho bu, familiyi bovom Simhoev shu.
e1809.en: Come, sit close to me. Listen to me. I'll tell you. My grandfather's name was Eliezer Simhaev. He was born in the city of Bukhara in 1840 to the family of Simha and Rivka. In the past people didn't have last names. His last name became Simhaev because his father was Simha.
e1809.speaker: Bivi

e1810.bux: Shumo gufta budet, ki bovoton a shari Qüqon bu.
e1810.en: You had told me that your grandfather was from the city of Kokand.
e1810.speaker: Navera

e1811.bux: Hov, ba'd ba soloyi yoshigeshon bovom ba Qüqon küchidin.
e1811.en: Yes, but then in his youth my grandfather moved to Kokand.
e1811.speaker: Bivi

e1812.en: What did he use to do there?
e1812.speaker: Navera

e1813.bux: Shon kori savdogari mekadin. Savdogari yakumi gildiya, odami boy-badavlat budin. Xudashon odami nek budin, chashmoyi kavüd va müyi mala doshtin.
e1813.en: He worked in commerce. He was a merchant of the First Guild, a very rich man. He himself was a kind person; he had green eyes and red hair.
e1813.speaker: Bivi

e1820.bux: A broyi hamin, musulmono ba ü nomi Malaboy dodan. Ma'noyi hamin laqam - boye ki müyi mala dora. Hamin nom qati bovom bisyor nomdor shudin.
e1820.en: That is why the Muslims gave him the name Malaboy. The meaning of this nickname is a wealthy man with red hair. He became well known by this name.
e1820.speaker: Bivi

e1821.en: Did you see your grandfather yourself?
e1821.speaker: Navera

e1822.bux: Ne. Ma bovoma nadidam, abaski ü ba'di inqilov ba soli 1921 ba Yerusholayim gurext. Lekin man medonam, ki bovom, Xudo rahmat karda bosha, joshon ba Gan-'Eden bosha, odamshavanda, misvodüst budin. Miyoni odamo bisyor ovrüyu 'izat doshtin. Panjo sol ü kalontari jamo'ati isroeli shari Qüqon budin. Ba'd xoneshonba universitet vo shud.
e1822.en: No, I didn't see my grandfather, because he fled to Jerusalem in 1921 after the revolution. But I know that my grandfather, may his soul rest in peace and his place be in Gan Eden, was a noble person and a benefactor. People respected him greatly. For fifty years he was the head of the Jewish community of the city of Kokand. Later a university was opened in his house.
e1822.speaker: Bivi

e1823.en: How many children did Malaboy have?
e1823.speaker: Navera

e1830.bux: Bovom, Malaboy, bivim Rohel Uvadeva qati hafta bacha doshtin: Aboyi Mala, Bulür, Imosholüm, Miryom, Yahudo-Ari (Meli) - dadim, Isroel, Baxmal. Abo 'amakam odami nek, boy-badavlat, odamshavanda, asilzoda, savdogari gildiyi yakum budin, chandta fabriku zavod doshtin. Ba juuto yordam medodin, lekin qartaboz bu. Zanash, Bitiyo, duxtari Hayim Vadyaev bu. Duta 'amom ba duta farzandoyi Vadyaefo rasidan. Miryom ba Sion ben Hayim Vadyaev va Baxmal ba Rafoel ben Isok-Borux Vadyaev.
e1830.en: My grandfather Malaboy with my grandmother Rachel Uvadeva had seven children: Aboi Mala, Bulur, Imashalom, Miriam, my father Yehuda-Ari (Meli), Israel, and Bakhmal. My uncle Abo was a kind, rich, noble person, an aristocrat, a merchant of the First Guild, and had several factories. He was helping the Jews, but was a gambler. His wife Betty was a daughter of Hayim Wadiaef. Both of my aunts married Wadiaef sons: Miriam married Sion son of Haim Wadiaef and Bakhmal married Rafael son of Izhak-Baruch Wadiaef.
e1830.speaker: Bivi

e1831.en: Did all of them live in Kokand?
e1831.speaker: Navera

e1832.bux: Hov. Joni bivesh, tu hole yosh, lekin don ki bisyortarini mishpohoyi boyi savdogaro Qüqonba meshishtan. Akayu uka Vadyaefo a hama juuto boyi kalon budan, ba'd Rafoel Potelyahov va ba'd Simhaefo. Ino, seta mishpohoyi 'osheri godül miyoneshon qarchi qudo shudan.
e1832.en: Yes. My dear, you are still young, but know that most of the rich merchant families lived in Kokand. The richest among the Bukharian Jews were the Wadiaef brothers, then Rafael Poteliakhov, and then the Simhaevs. These three rich families became double in-laws with each other.
e1832.speaker: Bivi

e1833.en: From which family was your mother?
e1833.speaker: Navera

e1844.bux: Onim, rahmati, a Toshkan budin. Ü duxtari boyi Toshkan - Isoxor Davidov va Bonu Abramov (a avloti Qirq Qiz). Unvaxt odamoyi boy miyoni xudashon qudo meshudan. Haminxel onim a Toshkan ba Qüqon raftin. Xosgori ino Rayhoni Bulbul Yagudaev bu.
e1844.en: My late mother was from Tashkent. She was a daughter of a rich man of Tashkent - Isachar Davidov - and Bonu Abramov (from the family of the 40 Girls). In that time rich people used to marry among themselves. That is how my mother went from Tashkent to Kokand. Their matchmaker was Rayhon Bulbul (Nightingale) Yagudaev.
e1844.speaker: Bivi

e1845.bux: Rahmat bivijon. Gavaton bisyor qiziq. Aknun ma famidam: ki mo hastim va a gjo omadim.
e1845.en: Thanks, dear grandmother. Your story was very interesting. Now I know who we are and where we're from.
e1845.speaker: Navera

e920.en: As crooked tree will not be straight, a mother-in-law will not be a friend of her daughter-in-law.

e921.bux: Har chi kuni ba xud kuni, Xoh nek kuni, xoh bad kuni.
e921.en: Whatever you do, you do it for yourself, no matter it is good or bad.

e924.bux: Ha, mulo Hiskiyo, sholüm! Chitüyet? Ma shumoya du sol nadidam.
e924.en: Hey, Mr. Hisqiyo, hello! How are you? I didn't see you for two years.
e924.speaker: Rahamim

e925.bux: Sholüm, mulo Rahamim! Ma naghzam. Borux Hashem yak ma pesh zan giriftam. Hozir ma zannok.
e925.en: Hello Mr. Rahamim. I'm good. Thanks G-d I got married one month ago. Now I'm a married person.
e925.speaker: Hisqiyo

e926.bux: Mazoltüv, ma nafamidam-ku. Zanaton a kadom avlot?
e926.en: Congratulations, I didn't know that. From which clan is your wife?
e926.speaker: Rahamim

e928.bux: Zanam a avloti Moshe Kalontar, nomash Tomor.
e928.en: My wife is from the family of Moshe Kalontar, her name is Tamara.
e928.speaker: Hisqiyo

e929.bux: Hay-hay, ma zanatona meshinosam-ku. Ü duxtari Dovidi Kalontar va Shüshanoyi Muloqand meshü. Ino odamshavanda hastan.
e929.en: Wow, I know your wife. She is a daughter of David Kalontar and Shoshana Mulloqand. They are noble people.
e929.speaker: Rahamim

e930.bux: Hov, rosangi. Xay, chi gavoyi toza?
e930.speaker: Hisqiyo

e931.bux: Ma naghzam, Xudoba shukur. Yak sol pesh zan giriftam a avloti Aroni Qandin. Nomi ü Davüro. Yakta pisar doram - Ariel.
e931.en: I'm good, thanks God. I got married a year ago. She is from the family of Aharon Qandin. Her name is Debora. I have a son - Ariel.
e931.speaker: Rahamim

e932.en: Congratulations! May your son be happy!
e932.speaker: Hisqiyo
